walkthroughs.h2: Total war and the home front
walkthroughs.body_html:
Both World Wars were total wars.

Governments rationed food, directed industry and conscripted soldiers. Women filled jobs in munitions, farming and nursing. In WWII the Blitz bombed British cities — civilians became targets.

The Treaty of Versailles in 1919 forced Germany to accept war guilt, pay reparations and lose territory and forces.

After WWII the Allies tried Nazi leaders at Nuremberg and set up the United Nations in 1945 to prevent another world war.

WWII killed around 70-85 million people, including six million Jewish victims of the Holocaust.

Empires collapsed, the USA and USSR became superpowers, and the world entered the Cold War. Decolonisation followed across Asia and Africa.

mcqs.q: Why did the Schlieffen Plan fail in 1914?
options: The Schlieffen Plan failed because Britain entered the war.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Belgian resistance delayed the German advance; Russia mobilised faster than expected; Moltke weakened the right wing; and the French rallied at the Marne.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
